subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should OpenClaw allow SKILL.md metadata to declare autonomous schedule/event triggers, and what operator approval, provenance, and revocation boundary must gate that execution?
rationale: This would turn installed skill metadata into a source of future agent execution, which is a public product and security contract rather than a mechanical parser change.

options.title: Design a gated trigger contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer-approved metadata shape, trust model, audit state, and explicit operator enablement before implementation.

options.title: Start with documentation-only metadata
options.body: Allow a non-executing trigger_description or ClawHub indexing field first, leaving cron registration manual until the security model is settled.

options.title: Reject SKILL.md execution triggers
options.body: Keep autonomous scheduling as explicit cron/plugin configuration only and use docs or ClawHub guidance for self-documenting skills.

recommendation.title: Design a gated trigger contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require maintainer-approved metadata shape, trust model, audit state, and explicit operator enablement before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, plugin/skill scope, and cron behavior where this person has broad recent repository history.
